*Chunk 1*: Loading the required packages, including the tidyverse for data manipulation. Although I loaded terra and sf -- as I intended to do some more spatial analysis than I ultimately was able to peform -- I did not use them. 

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(terra)
library(sf)
```

*Chunk 2*: In this chunk, I utilized Dr. Shannon's script to read in the numbats data and weather data (using the weatherOz package). It appears that this chunk works to first manipulate the numbats data -- including via the addition of a 0 to the month data to put it in a format consistent with the weather data. From there, weather data is extracted using the SILO API to get a more complete record of weather data -- given that the weather data provided in the numbat sightings is very incomplete. After that, an attempt was made to join the weather and numbat datasets; however, the lack of an exact-matching field with which the join could be peformed made this task difficult (and thus it was not completed).  

```{r}
#Using Dr. Shannon's script to get wx data in:

install.packages("weatherOz")
library(weatherOz)

numbat_data<-read_csv("data/numbats.csv") %>%
  filter(!is.na(eventDate)) %>%
  mutate(event_oz=paste0(year(eventDate),
                         str_pad(month(eventDate),2,pad="0"),
                         str_pad(day(eventDate),2,pad="0")))
summary(numbat_data)

x <- get_data_drill(
  longitude  = 153.0,
  latitude   = -27.5,
  start_date = "20240101",
  end_date   = "20241231",
  values     = c("max_temp", "min_temp", "rain"),
  api_key    = "jshannon@uga.edu"
)

numbat_wx<-function(row_sel){
  numbat_sel<-numbat_data[row_sel,]
  
  get_data_drill(
    longitude=numbat_sel$decimalLongitude,
    latitude=numbat_sel$decimalLatitude,
    start_date=numbat_sel$event_oz,
    end_date=numbat_sel$event_oz,
    values     = c("max_temp", "min_temp", "rain"),
    api_key    = "jshannon@uga.edu"
  ) %>%
    rename(decimalLatitude=latitude,
           decimalLongitude=longitude,)
}

#nrow_plus1 <- nrow(numbat_data) + 1 #Did not work, was trying to experiment with the dates

weather_data<-map_df(1:nrow(numbat_data),possibly(numbat_wx))
#numbat_wx<-numbat_data %>%
  #rename(date=day) %>%
  #left_join(weather_data)

```

```{R}
#Trying to plot the data for numbat sightings vs. precip (in some way)

#Without the weather_data, just the wx data in numbat_data

numbats_cleaned <- numbat_data %>%
  filter(prcp != "NA") %>%
  filter(tmax != "NA") %>%
  mutate(tmax_corr = tmax/10)

ggplot(numbats_cleaned,
       aes(x=prcp, 
           y=tmax_corr)) +
  geom_point() +
  ggtitle("Precip and Max Temp Obs for Numbat Sightings") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 11)) +
  xlab("Mean Precip (mm)") +
  ylab("Mean Maximum Temp (°C)") #Had to do this to capitilize "region" in the legend. 

```
```{R}
#Plotting the wx_data

ggplot(weather_data,
       aes(x=rainfall, 
           y=air_tmax)) +
  geom_point() +
  ggtitle("Precip and Max Temp Obs (Overall Weather Dataset)") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 11)) +
  xlab("Mean Precip (mm)") +
  ylab("Mean Maximum Temp (°C)") #Had to do this to capitilize "region" in the legend. 
```
```{R}
#Trying to plot the numbat obs on a map of Australia to prove the obvious -- numbats are found in desert areas that, unsurprisingly, do not get much rain. 

australia_borders <- st_read("data/AUSTRALIA SHAPEFILE/AUSTRALIA_Shapefiles/Australia_adm/Australia_adm01.shp") %>%
  st_transform(4326)

australia_borders <- map_data("world",region = "Australia")

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data=australia_borders,
               aes(x=long,
                   y=lat,
                   group=group,
                   alpha=0.5)) +
  geom_point(data=numbat_data,
             aes(x=decimalLongitude,
                 y=decimalLatitude)) +
  guides(alpha = "none") +
  labs(title = "Numbat Sightings in Australia")

```

Response: For this activity, I utilized the numbats dataset we chose in class. This dataset includes data on numbat sightings across Australia, including their location, scientific name, date, and a limited amount of weather data (like temp and precip). 

The research question I was attempting to answer was examining the relationship between numbat sightings and weather conditions. My original question was trying to just evaluate the relationship between numbats and precip amounts; however, I pivoted to the above mentioned question (looking at the broader relationship between numbat sightings and weather observations). Specifically, I eventually attempted to answer whether there is any difference in temp and precip distribution for numbat sightings compared to the overall temp and precip distribution.
